subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: Should the durable memory lifecycle be owned now by a maintainer-sponsored memory-core/Memory Audit design, or deferred until the schema and write-pipeline MVP issues are settled?
rationale: This is a broad product and data-model decision touching persistence, privacy, operator UX, migration, and the relationship between Dreaming, Memory Audit, and memory-wiki; automation cannot safely choose the canonical lifecycle contract.

options.title: Sponsor canonical lifecycle design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require a maintainer-approved design tying schema, write pipeline, Memory Audit, CLI/UI, and migration behavior together.

options.title: Narrow to Memory Audit PR
options.body: Treat the draft Memory Audit PR as the first landing path, but leave this issue open until it covers edit/forget/conflict behavior or splits follow-up issues.

options.title: Defer the lifecycle MVP
options.body: Leave existing dreaming and memory-wiki surfaces in place and wait until the underlying schema/write pipeline work is ready.

recommendation.title: Sponsor canonical lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require a maintainer-approved design tying schema, write pipeline, Memory Audit, CLI/UI, and migration behavior together.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent memory docs/promotion history and was mentioned in the issue timeline, making him the best available routing owner from the inspected history.
